endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: At minimum, organizations must identify who is responsible for oversight, validation, monitoring, and data stewardship.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: It is vital to have qualified health care personnel in the loop, and patient/caregiver representatives when they may be end users.

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: This team could include individuals with the following expertise as appropriate: executive leadership, regulatory/ ethical compliance, information technology (IT), safety/ incident reporting, relevant clinical/operational expertise, cybersecurity and data privacy needs, and stakeholders reflecting the needs of impacted populations (e.g., staff, providers, patients, caregivers, etc.).

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement
endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)
endorsements.quote: Addressing ethical issues in AI will require a combination of technical solutions, government activity, regulatory oversight, and ethical guidelines developed in collaboration with a wide range of stakeholders, including clinicians, patients, AI developers, and ethicists.

endorsements.title: Implementing the human right to science in the regulatory governance of artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.issuer: Journal of law and the biosciences
endorsements.quote: In order to advance ML and to account for a wider range of actual uses that AIMDs could be applied toward, regulatory governance will need to be more participatory in actively and meaningfully involving patients, healthcare providers, and other users or operators.

endorsements.title: Ethical use of big data for healthy communities and a strong nation: unique challenges for the Military Health System
endorsements.quote: A community advisory panel whose contributions are valued can improve the research process, flag potential abuses, and approve secondary uses of data when appropriate.

endorsements.title: EyeMatics: An Ophthalmology Use Case Within the German Medical Informatics Initiative
endorsements.quote: The governance of the consortium consists of the Management Board (MB) that includes an interplay of patient representatives (n=2); domain experts in clinical ophthalmology, epidemiology, and basic biomedical science (n=6); and experts in biomedical informatics (n=5).

endorsements.title: Pathology in the artificial intelligence era: Guiding innovation and implementation to preserve human insight
endorsements.quote: This could include establishing pathologist-led advisory boards to oversee AI applications, forming dedicated research partnerships with AI developers to ensure that patient outcomes and clinical needs are prioritized and creating continuous feedback channels that allow pathologists to adapt AI systems according to evolving clinical and ethical considerations.

endorsements.title: A participatory approach to deploy responsible artificial intelligence for diabetes prediction and prevention
endorsements.quote: To steer this process, Phase 1 involves establishing a partnership table that includes senior leaders from the provincial government health care agencies; clinicians from local hospitals, primary care networks and family health teams; community-based organizations and public health agencies; as well as patients and caregivers with lived experience of Type 2 diabetes and the healthcare system.

endorsements.title: Reframing Justice in Healthcare AI: An Ubuntu-Based Approach for Africa
endorsements.quote: For African healthcare, ethics committees should include patient advocates, nurses, and community health workers to ensure AI governance reflects the realities of those who directly deliver and receive care.

endorsements.title: Perspective on patient and non-academic partner engagement for the responsible integration of large language models in health chatbots
endorsements.quote: Adopting inclusive governance through multidisciplinary and diverse boards can address ethical considerations, uncover blind spots, and foster inclusive design.

endorsements.title: A call for ethical, equitable, and effective artificial intelligence to improve care for all people with epilepsy: A roadmap. A report by the ILAE Global Advocacy Council and Big Data Commission
endorsements.quote: AI‐based projects should involve people with lived experience in all phases of the research and deployment process.

endorsements.title: Bridging the governance gap in health artificial intelligence: integrating nursing perspectives into the National Academy of Medicine Artificial Intelligence Code of Conduct
endorsements.issuer: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
endorsements.quote: Form a multidisciplinary AI governance committee. Explicitly include nursing leaders, physicians, data scientists, IT professionals, compliance professionals, and patient/family representatives.

endorsements.title: The Ethics of Leveraging Routinely Collected Patient Data for AI Development: Mixed Methods Study
endorsements.quote: Embed patient representatives (ideally trained in AI ethics and data governance) in ethics committees and regulatory boards to strengthen inclusiveness and transparency in oversight processes.

endorsements.title: Ethical Governance of Artificial Intelligence in Cardiovascular Disease Management: A Health Policy Perspective
endorsements.quote: Furthermore, health systems must establish multidisciplinary AI ethics committees composed of cardiologists, data scientists, and community patient advocates to provide human-in-the-loop surveillance of AI outputs.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence and nursing science: Opportunities, challenges, implications, and guidelines
endorsements.quote: These interdisciplinary AI working groups should also have a balanced representation from other domains, including academics from both STEM fields and humanities, industry professionals from informatics and data science, regulatory bodies, administrative leadership, and patients or their advocates if applicable.

endorsements.title: Foundation for Artificial Intelligence-Driven Democratization of Healthcare Access
endorsements.quote: Healthcare governance authorities must establish independent AI ethics review boards characterized by diverse stakeholder representation, encompassing multidisciplinary expertise from clinical specialties, technical disciplines, legal domains, and patient advocacy perspectives [ 17 ].

endorsements.title: Centering the marginalized: AI-driven strategies for advancing health equity in rare disease care
endorsements.quote: Multidisciplinary governance bodies, comprising clinicians, ethicists, patient advocates, and policymakers, should guide resource allocation through rigorous cost-utility analyses that prioritize unmet needs.

endorsements.title: Discursive Ethics as a Normative Foundation for Integrating Ethics into AI Clinical Decision Support Systems
endorsements.quote: Xivuri and Twinomurinzi ( 2022 ) and Rehg ( 2015 ) agree that individuals affected by AI algorithms or by decisions made by AI algorithms should be involved in the planning and development stages of AI algorithms.

endorsements.title: Moving beyond the benchmarks: Five foundational principles for meaningful AI evaluation in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Ensure institutional review board includes community representatives, not just academic physicians

endorsements.title: Real-World Data Needs Real-World Doctors: When Automation Advances Faster Than Clinical Workflow
endorsements.quote: To ensure AI implementation truly serves those it is meant to help, we recommend fully compensated [ 18 ] “patient” and “clinician-in-the-loop” team roles, with genuine voting power over co-created outcomes.

endorsements.title: Establishing a framework for development, prioritization, and assessment of artificial intelligence technology within the radiology department at a large UK teaching hospital
endorsements.quote: The AI board works in partnership with a patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) body.

endorsements.title: Achieving Equity in Generative Artificial Intelligence in Cardiovascular Medicine
endorsements.quote: It is essential to establish cross-functional AI governance committees in health care systems that include representatives from all stakeholders, such as clinical leadership, information technology, compliance, patient safety, privacy, frontline clinicians, and the community.

endorsements.title: Driving global health equity with artificial intelligence: the global initiative on AI for health (GI-AI4H)
endorsements.quote: forming inclusive data governance committees

endorsements.title: Equity-centred, nurse-led implementation of artificial intelligence in community maternal and child health nursing: a conceptual framework for low-resource settings
endorsements.quote: Nurses should contribute systematically to AI system design, workflow integration, community engagement, policy development and outcome evaluation.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this recommendation tests whether adding patient, caregiver, or community representatives to AI governance bodies changes governance decisions or patient outcomes. Support rests on 25 endorsing sources, most of them commentaries, and none documents the hazard empirically.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice and zero studies document the hazard. The endorsements consist of frameworks, guidance, and commentaries that state expert opinion. One commentary describes a consortium board with 2 patient representatives, but it reports no outcomes. Under GRADE conventions, expert opinion without comparative data cannot support a certainty rating above no direct evidence.

The strongest endorsement language comes from the CHAI playbooks, which use "must." The quoted text requires naming who holds oversight roles and does not name patients. The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide limits patient representation to cases where patients may be end users. The RUAIH guidance uses "may." These sources suggest that patient membership is an expectation that sources state with varying force.

commentary.research_gap: No supplied study compares governance committees with and without patient or community members on measurable results such as which tools are approved or rejected, how often bias or safety concerns are raised, or how patients later report trust. Studies are also needed on how representatives are recruited, supported, and compensated, and on whether their input changes decisions or remains advisory.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of the practice exists, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Several commentaries call for community health workers, community-based organizations, or people with lived experience on governance bodies. Whether representatives drawn from these groups change decisions affecting them remains untested.
